universal_lens: A structural gate operator that enforces epistemic integrity by refusing inference on unconfirmed fixtures, formalizing the boundary between verified reality and hallucinated analysis through slate-membership verification and fiction-discrimination predicates. Universal Lens: Rooted in CHI@ATL-card-REFUSED (f83c575e9d636760), this derivation preserves strict unit consistency, explicit validity boundaries, zero-leakage temporal separation, and bounded structural integration across GSI calibration heads, spectral orthogonalization clusters, and GSE Stage-2 situational reasoning families without fabricating parameters.
gsi_mapping: Maps to a Bayesian prior over fixture existence: P(fixture ∈ slate | evidence) → 0 triggers hard refusal. The conformal layer emits a non-conformity score of 1.0 for unconfirmed matchups, vetoing any posterior predictive distribution.
gse_mapping: Implements a state-transition guard: current_state = {slate_confirmed: false} → action = REFUSE. primitives.name: Fixture Confirmation Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: # CHI@ATL - FIXTURE NOT CONFIRMED (card REFUSED) **This matchup is not a game on the real 6 slate.** The engine does not emit an analyst card for a fixture it cannot confirm.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: slate ∈ {confirmed, unconfirmed} (dimensionless); emit_card ∈ {0,1} (dimensionless); fixture_id ∈ string (dimensionless); period ∈ ℕ (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Engine has access to authoritative slate data for period; fixture identity is resolvable; confirmation is binary and deterministic.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Slate data source unavailable or ambiguous; period mapping non-injective; fixture_id collision across periods.

layer2.mapping: GSE: State-transition guard δ(s, a) where s.slate_confirmed = false → a = REFUSE. GSI: Prior P(H₀: fixture_real) = 0 induces infinite KL divergence from any analytic posterior.
layer2.telemetry: Refusal rate per period; false refusal rate (fixture actually on slate but missed); latency of slate ingestion.

primitives.name: Fiction-Analysis Discriminator
primitives.verbatim_quote: A card here would be fiction that reads as analysis.
primitives.assumptions: Fiction and analysis are distinguishable by provenance; any output on unconfirmed fixture is necessarily fiction; the discriminator is a hard threshold at fiction_score > 0.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Adversarial mimicry where fiction simulates analysis provenance; semantic drift in 'analysis' definition; partial confirmation (e.g., teams known, time unknown).

layer2.mapping: GSI: Conformal p-value = 0 for any prediction on unconfirmed fixture → automatic rejection. GSE: Integrity monitor raises veto signal when output_generator(fixture ∉ slate) activates.
layer2.telemetry: Fiction detection precision/recall; human audit disagreement rate; downstream decision contamination incidents.

primitives.name: Slate Membership Verifier
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Why this card was refused - FIXTURE NOT ON SLATE: CHI@ATL is not a game in None (period 6).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: slate_set(period) ⊂ Fixture × Period (dimensionless); membership ∈ {true, false} (dimensionless); opponent_map: Team → Team ∪ {unknown} (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Slate_set is complete and accurate for period; team identifiers are canonical; 'unknown' opponent is a valid sentinel value.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Schedule changes post-publication; neutral-site games misassigned; team relocation/renaming not reflected in slate_set.

layer2.mapping: GSE: Membership check is a state predicate guard. GSI: Likelihood P(data | fixture ∈ slate) = 0 → posterior collapses. The 'unknown' opponent maps to maximal entropy over opponent space.
layer2.telemetry: Slate completeness metric; opponent resolution rate; period alignment error count.

primitives.name: Remediation Router
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## What to do instead - Re-run against the actual game (the real opponents are named above).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: remediation_action ∈ {re_run(actual_fixture), adjust_period(periodId)} (dimensionless); actual_fixture ∈ Fixture (dimensionless); periodId ∈ ℕ (dimensionless); routing_policy: Error → Action (dimensionless)
primitives.assumptions: Actual opponents are recoverable from context; periodId mapping is bijective for the fixture; user can supply correct period.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Actual opponents not named in context; fixture belongs to no period (exhibition/cancelled); periodId collision across seasons.

layer2.mapping: GSE: Corrective transition function τ: (error_state, context) → valid_state. GSI: Active learning query — requests minimal sufficient statistic (periodId or actual_fixture) to restore identifiability.
layer2.telemetry: Remediation success rate; user compliance rate; time-to-valid-card after remediation.

The primitives form a closed loop: (1) Slate Membership Verifier checks fixture ∈ slate_set(period). Failure → (2) Fixture Confirmation Gate blocks emission (emit_card=0). Simultaneously, (3) Fiction-Analysis Discriminator assigns fiction_score=1 to any hypothetical output, locking epistemic_integrity=compromised if bypassed. Finally, (4) Remediation Router computes the minimal corrective action: either substitute actual_fixture from context or shift periodId. Mathematically, this is a guard-railed inference pipeline where the state space of valid analyses is exactly the preimage of slate_set under the fixture-period projection. The 'unknown' opponent sentinel in quote 4 induces a uniform prior over opponent space, maximizing entropy and minimizing mutual information between any predicted statistic and reality — a formal justification for refusal. The breakdown regimes expose the system's dependence on slate_set completeness and canonical identifiers; adversarial schedule manipulation or data latency could induce false refusals or, worse, false confirmations. The duality between GSE (state-transition guards) and GSI (conformal veto) is exact: both compute a binary acceptability predicate from the same membership oracle.
